## Dataset provenance

This vignette uses real TCGA-BRCA example objects prepared for OmicsKit from
UCSC Xena TCGA-BRCA inputs. The heavy data preparation is performed outside the
vignette in `data-raw/brca/`, and the vignette only loads package-ready objects
from `data/` and displays prerendered figures from `vignettes/figures/`.

The RNA-seq DEA objects are derived from Xena log2-normalized HiSeqV2
expression. The RPPA/proteomics objects are derived from a TCGA-BRCA RPPA
matrix with feature-to-gene mappings preserved only when available from the
input annotations. No Xena downloads, limma model fitting, or matrix filtering
are run in this vignette.

```{r packages}
library(OmicsKit)
```

```{r load_brca_objects}
data(brca_metadata)
data(brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg)
data(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal)
data(brca_rna_metadata_er_shared)
data(brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal)
data(brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small)
data(brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg)
data(brca_rppa_expr_gene_er_shared)

list(
  metadata_samples = nrow(brca_metadata),
  rna_er_genes = nrow(brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg),
  rna_tumor_normal_genes = nrow(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal),
  rppa_gene_features = nrow(brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg)
)
```

## Comparisons

Two real TCGA-BRCA comparisons are provided.

The first comparison is **Tumor vs Normal** using RNA-seq only. Tumor and
normal samples are identified from TCGA sample type metadata, including TCGA
sample code where needed. This comparison does not require RPPA availability.

The second comparison is **ER_positive vs ER_negative** in primary tumors. For
the RNA-seq ER comparison, the prepared example uses primary tumor samples with
matched RNA and RPPA identifiers so that RNA and protein results can be compared
consistently downstream.

```{r comparison_counts}
table(brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal$rna_tumor_normal, useNA = "ifany")
table(brca_rna_metadata_er_shared$ER_group, useNA = "ifany")
```

## RNA-seq DEA using limma

RNA-seq DEA was run with limma on the Xena log2-normalized expression matrix.
The preparation script filters low-expression genes, removes zero-variance
genes, collapses duplicated gene symbols by mean, and collapses duplicated
sample columns after TCGA barcode trimming.

For the ER comparison, the reference group is `ER_negative`, and the contrast is
`ER_positive - ER_negative`. Therefore, `logFC > 0` means higher expression in
ER-positive primary tumors.

For Tumor vs Normal, the reference group is `Normal`, and `logFC > 0` means
higher expression in tumor samples.

```{r rna_dea_summary}
rna_er_sig <- sum(brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
rna_tn_sig <- sum(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

data.frame(
  comparison = c("ER_positive_vs_ER_negative", "Tumor_vs_Normal"),
  n_features = c(
    nrow(brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg),
    nrow(brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal)
  ),
  n_fdr_lt_0_05 = c(rna_er_sig, rna_tn_sig)
)
```

```{r rna_limma_generation, eval = FALSE}
# Heavy processing lives in data-raw/brca/02_prepare_transcriptomics_dea_brca.R.
# The vignette does not rerun this code.
#
# Source inputs:
# - inst/extdata/brca/raw_xena/TCGA.BRCA.sampleMap_HiSeqV2/HiSeqV2
# - data/brca_metadata.rda
#
# Output objects:
# - brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg
# - brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal
# - brca_rna_expr_er_shared_filtered
# - brca_rna_expr_tumor_normal_filtered
# - brca_rna_metadata_er_shared
# - brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal
# - brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small
```

## RPPA/proteomics DEA using limma

The RPPA/proteomics DEA example uses real TCGA-BRCA RPPA measurements for the
ER-positive vs ER-negative primary tumor comparison. The same contrast direction
is used as RNA-seq: `ER_positive - ER_negative`, so `logFC > 0` indicates higher
RPPA signal in ER-positive tumors.

Only explicit feature-to-gene mappings are used for the gene-level RPPA object.
Feature mappings are not inferred in the vignette.

```{r rppa_dea_summary}
rppa_sig <- sum(brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg$padj < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)

data.frame(
  comparison = "ER_positive_vs_ER_negative",
  n_features = nrow(brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg),
  n_fdr_lt_0_05 = rppa_sig
)
```

```{r rppa_limma_generation, eval = FALSE}
# Heavy processing lives in data-raw/brca/03_prepare_proteomics_dea_brca.R.
# The vignette does not rerun this code.
#
# Source inputs:
# - inst/extdata/brca/raw_xena/[RPPA matrix file]
# - data/brca_metadata.rda
#
# Output objects:
# - brca_rppa_dea_feature_er_pos_vs_er_neg
# - brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg
# - brca_rppa_expr_feature_er_shared
# - brca_rppa_expr_gene_er_shared
# - brca_rppa_feature_map
```

## nice_Volcano examples

`nice_Volcano()` visualizes differential analysis results using effect size on
the x-axis and FDR on the y-axis. The figures below are prerendered from the
real BRCA DEA objects.

```{r volcano_rna_er_code, eval = FALSE}
nice_Volcano(
  results   = brca_rna_dea_er_pos_vs_er_neg,
  x_var     = "logFC",
  y_var     = "padj",
  label_var = "gene_symbol",
  title     = "RNA-seq: ER-positive vs ER-negative",
  cutoff_y  = 0.05,
  cutoff_x  = 1
)
```

```{r volcano_rna_er_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq DEA: ER-positive vs ER-negative primary tumors. Positive logFC indicates higher expression in ER-positive tumors.", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_volcano_rna_er_pos_vs_er_neg.png")
```

```{r volcano_rna_tn_code, eval = FALSE}
nice_Volcano(
  results   = brca_rna_dea_tumor_vs_normal,
  x_var     = "logFC",
  y_var     = "padj",
  label_var = "gene_symbol",
  title     = "RNA-seq: Tumor vs Normal",
  cutoff_y  = 0.05,
  cutoff_x  = 1
)
```

```{r volcano_rna_tn_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq DEA: Tumor vs Normal. Positive logFC indicates higher expression in tumor samples.", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_volcano_rna_tumor_vs_normal.png")
```

```{r volcano_rppa_er_code, eval = FALSE}
nice_Volcano(
  results   = brca_rppa_dea_gene_er_pos_vs_er_neg,
  x_var     = "logFC",
  y_var     = "padj",
  label_var = "gene",
  title     = "RPPA: ER-positive vs ER-negative",
  cutoff_y  = 0.05,
  cutoff_x  = 0.20
)
```

```{r volcano_rppa_er_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "TCGA-BRCA RPPA DEA: ER-positive vs ER-negative primary tumors. Positive logFC indicates higher RPPA signal in ER-positive tumors.", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_volcano_rppa_er_pos_vs_er_neg.png")
```

## nice_VSB examples

`nice_VSB()` displays gene- or feature-level values across sample groups using
violin, scatter, and boxplot layers. These examples use real prepared RNA-seq
and RPPA matrices and are displayed as prerendered figures.

```{r vsb_rna_code, eval = FALSE}
nice_VSB(
  object      = brca_rna_expr_er_shared_filtered,
  annotations = brca_rna_metadata_er_shared,
  variables   = c(fill = "ER_group"),
  genename    = "ESR1",
  categories  = c("ER_negative", "ER_positive"),
  labels      = c("ER-", "ER+"),
  colors      = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
  shapes      = 21,
  markersize  = 3
)
```

```{r vsb_rna_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "ESR1 RNA-seq expression across ER-negative and ER-positive TCGA-BRCA primary tumors.", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_vsb_rna_ESR1.png")
```

```{r vsb_rppa_code, eval = FALSE}
nice_VSB(
  object      = brca_rppa_expr_gene_er_shared,
  annotations = brca_rna_metadata_er_shared,
  variables   = c(fill = "ER_group"),
  genename    = "ERBB2",
  categories  = c("ER_negative", "ER_positive"),
  labels      = c("ER-", "ER+"),
  colors      = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
  shapes      = 21,
  markersize  = 3
)
```

```{r vsb_rppa_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "ERBB2 RPPA signal across ER-negative and ER-positive TCGA-BRCA primary tumors.", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_vsb_rppa_ERBB2.png")
```

## Unsupervised transcriptomic visualization

The object `brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small` contains the top 1000 variable genes
from the ER-positive vs ER-negative RNA-seq matrix. It is intentionally compact
so the package can demonstrate `nice_PCA()`, `nice_UMAP()`, and `nice_tSNE()`
without shipping a large full expression matrix.

The rendered figures below use ER status as the sample annotation.

```{r dimred_code, eval = FALSE}
metadata_dim <- brca_rna_metadata_er_shared
metadata_dim$id <- rownames(metadata_dim)

nice_PCA(
  object       = brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small,
  annotations  = metadata_dim,
  variables    = c(fill = "ER_group"),
  legend_names = c(fill = "ER status"),
  colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick")
)

nice_UMAP(
  object       = brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small,
  annotations  = metadata_dim,
  variables    = c(fill = "ER_group"),
  legend_names = c(fill = "ER status"),
  colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
  seed         = 2025
)

nice_tSNE(
  object       = brca_rna_vst_or_logexpr_small,
  annotations  = metadata_dim,
  variables    = c(fill = "ER_group"),
  legend_names = c(fill = "ER status"),
  colors       = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
  seed         = 2025
)
```

```{r pca_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "PCA of compact TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq expression matrix, colored by ER status.", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_pca_rna_er_status.png")
```

```{r umap_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "UMAP of compact TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq expression matrix, colored by ER status.", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_umap_rna_er_status.png")
```

```{r tsne_plot, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "t-SNE of compact TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq expression matrix, colored by ER status.", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/brca_tsne_rna_er_status.png")
```

## Notes on trend_filter

`trend_filter()` is designed for paired or ordered comparisons where the sample
relationships have been explicitly validated. The BRCA Tumor vs Normal example
in this vignette is prepared as a group-level DEA example, and the required
paired tumor-normal relationships have not been fully validated here.

For that reason, the example below is shown as non-executed code only. Validate
patient pairing and sample ordering before using it in an analysis.

```{r trend_filter_note, eval = FALSE}
# Example only: do not run until paired tumor-normal requirements are validated.
#
# paired_metadata <- brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal[
#   order(brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal$patient,
#         brca_rna_metadata_tumor_normal$rna_tumor_normal),
# ]
#
# trend_filter(
#   object = brca_rna_expr_tumor_normal_filtered,
#   metadata = paired_metadata,
#   group_col = "rna_tumor_normal",
#   patient_col = "patient"
# )
```
